I mean the traffic violation, it does not affect order and discipline in the Split Military District. So Gotovina, the non-organic commander, decides to forward to the organic commander, i.e., the commander of the 7th Guards Brigade. I hope that that explains the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If can I add, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, as long as you don't give evidence, Mr. Waespi, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: It's just a follow-up of the previous document we looked at. It's the reporting back to P1020 so even in itself, and there's been no objection to 1020 -- the foundation is laid, if you want, from a formalistic point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And the fact that P1020 was introduced, the opposite proposition was put forward which is part of why I'm now surprised that the counterproposition is being offered by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- for the time being. This document will be marked for identification. We'll look at it and see whether there 's sufficient relevance to have it admitted into evidence. Madam Registrar, was a number already assigned. I think it was not. No. Could you please do it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit number P1118, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it keeps that status for the time being. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let's move on to P1014. Can you briefly explain what the document is about and the significance, if any?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is just 1014 not P, but maybe I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think it is a P.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm sorry. This is an another implementation of Article 26 whereby, here, the non-organic commander considers that the violation of discipline by members of a unit which is temporarily subordinated to him is of such a seriousness that he has to take the disciplinary measures immediately. The non-organic commander is General Gotovina. The unit which is temporarily subordinated, i.e., a non-organic unit, is the 2nd Infantry Battalion of the 9th Guards Brigade. This unit is also known under the name Termiti [phoen]and has also been known before as the 84th Guards Battalion. This is not mentioned in the document but ... So this document states: We are sending you enclosed orders on disciplinary measures imposed by the Split Military District commander to the following members of the HV 2nd Infantry Battalion of the 9th Guards Brigade. So Split Military District commander is the non-organic commander who has this unit, 2nd Infantry Battalion of the 9 Guards Brigade, temporarily subordinated to him. The 9 Guards Brigade belongs normally to the Gospic Military District. We can alos see that from the heading in the top left corner. And in the attachment, we can see -- which is actually the third English page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This document has been uploaded in e-court with two pages. From what I have -- if we are talking about the same document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the right document, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is the right document. Yes. That's another one we just had. Please proceed. You said the third page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, but this is the right page now because it is it probably uploaded than the form I have it in. When we go to the last page of this document we see that it is signed by General Gotovina, commander of the Split Military District. He submits it to a number of people, including the 9 Guards Brigade, to the attention of the 2nd Infantry Battalion of the 9 Guards Brigade. When we move back now to the first page, we see from the contents that General Gotovina has imposed a disciplinary measure against a member of the 9th -- excuse me, of the 2nd Battalion of the 9 Guards Brigade, and this disciplinary measure imposed by Gotovina can be found in the middle of the page. It is the disciplinary measure of military detention for duration of ten days. In my view, this is an implementation of Article 26 because the commander of the Split Military District has imposed a disciplinary measure against a member or an offender of a unit which is not an organic unit of his for a violation of discipline he considers important and for which he considers that it's -- yeah, that it is important to take urgent measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let's go to the next document, a new one, 65 ter 2425. And it's a document dated 20th July 1995. What's the significance again, Mr. Theunens, of this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an example of the implementation of the discipline system as well as also of the implementation of what is described as the concept of situational awareness, which is discussed in my report. That is that the commander obviously is responsible for the implementation of discipline, and in order to make sure that he takes care of that obligation, he, the commander of the Split Military District, requests his units to provide him with data, with information on the number of disciplinary procedures and measures they have taken or undertaken during the first half of 1995. On the second page of the document, of the English document, you can find the addressees. The units are identified by their military post number, and, for example, the fifth in the row, 2233, is the military post number of the 72nd Military Police Battalion, indicating that the 72nd Military Police Battalion is an organic unit of the Split Military District. The later pages in the document provide the template and the references for the information the subordinate units of the Split Military District have to provide to the Split Military District Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I would like it tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objection. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your HonourS, that will be Exhibit number 1119.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1119 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And perhaps, Mr. President, one more document before the break. This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you about one of the previous documents. They're always juggling with page numbers, et cetera. The documents in which we find the ten days of military confinement I think that was the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think P1014.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that there's an English translation of two pages whereas the original is seven pages. There must be something wrong there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It consists of several documents. It looks as if a letter announces three cases and that we find three two-page documents in which, at least in one of them, disciplinary measure is imposed, but there is in e-court supposed to be a second translation which is not there, apparently. Mr. Waespi, I'm not by -- for pleasure, establishing my image as a bookkeeper.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I will check overnight the status --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think the next document will be P1013.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: This is an existing exhibit already. Again, based on your analysis, review of the materials, what's the significance of this order dated 29th August 1995?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this set of documents is an example of the commander of the Split Military District using his authority as the Military District Commander to order measures in view of establishing criminal responsibility. It has to do with the illegal occupation of public housing or flats. On the first page, in paragraph 1, we can see that the commander of the Split Military District orders to appoint a commission for investigation consisting of a number of members, including the deputy commander of the 72nd Military Police Battalion. The commander of the Split Military District then, in paragraph 2, determines the tasks of this commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me ask you about the front page again. It states that the order was given pursuant to an order of the chief of the Croatian army Main Staff. Now, could Mr. Gotovina have issued this order on his own right or does he have to -- did he issue it pursuant to -- to -- did he have to wait for the authority given by his superior to issue this order?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, such a conclusion cannot be drawn from this document, but it is my understanding of the review of the other material that indeed the commander of a Military District has the authority to establish, for example, such commissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Objection. Lack of foundation, Your Honour. Nor was this disclosed in the expert report or at any other time by the Prosecution in 800 pages of material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, I take it that the lack of foundation relates to the second part of the answer not the first part of the answer where he says we cannot draw any conclusions from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you further explore on what the understanding --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I still have an objection to him offering an opinion -- in 800 pages -- we are using direct now to go into opinions that are not in an 800-page report. I have an objection to the lack of disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I haven't got the 800 pages so in my mind to know for sure that not such a thing appears anywhere. Mr. Waespi, would you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I can ask him. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- address the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: What 's the basis for you to say that the commander of the Military District had the authority to establish such commissions, irrespective of being ordered by his superior to do so?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And perhaps the first question whether you expressed any such an opinion at any place in your expert report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I base this conclusion on -- I think it is in the collection of documents here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's -- Mr. Misetic, what is your problem, apparently?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'd ask that he answer your question first, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The first question was whether such a conclusion appears anywhere in your expert report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. The conclusion does not appear as such in the expert report. I have not addressed specifically or have not mentioned specifically that a Military District Commander can establish a commission to investigate disciplinary issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I still have the objection then, Your Honour. I believe there is plenty of other material to cover without covering areas that have not been disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Well, the materials have all been disclosed. I'm quite certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But apparently the issue for Mr. Misetic is that if on the basis of disclosed material you could draw conclusions other than those we find in the report, that that should not be the subject because then the conclusion is not disclosed in the expert report, and I take it that many of the underlying documents would allow for conclusions of a totally different kind on matters. That apparently is the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Well, I think it is our position that there are areas or questions that this expert can address, or understand, without following each and every single opinion in -- in his report. That's just natural. And we believe that if the proper foundation is laid that he says, you know, what's the material he bases his -- or the doctrine he bases an opinion upon, that is sufficient to address the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider the matter but not today. Whether this is a question you may answer, Mr. Theunens, you'll hear from us tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same instruction as yesterday; you should not speak with anyone about the testimony whether already given or still to be given.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I want to be sure that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, Mr. Misetic wants to return publicly to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: On the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the record, yes. Meanwhile, I think copies have been made with the approval of the Trial Chamber we understood your permission to hand that over to the Prosecution that they were also able to copy it. If that is misunderstood, please tell us. We'll then adjourn until tomorrow, 9.00 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 21st day of November, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.
